"Create a complete 2D realistic survival RPG video game called \"ASHES OF TOMORROW\".

GAME CONCEPT:

The game takes place in 2041, five years after a devastating global war and the outbreak of an unknown biological infection. Civilization has collapsed. Cities are abandoned, governments no longer exist, and survivors struggle to find food, medicine, weapons, and shelter.

The player controls a young survivor trying to stay alive while discovering the truth behind the infection and the events that destroyed humanity.

VISUAL STYLE:

- 2D realistic graphics.
- Detailed environments and character animations.
- Dark, cinematic atmosphere.
- Realistic lighting and shadows.
- Abandoned buildings, destroyed vehicles, forests, military bases, and underground laboratories.
- Weather effects such as rain, fog, storms, and snow.
- Detailed character sprites with realistic proportions.
- Smooth movement and combat animations.
- High-quality environmental details.

GAMEPLAY MECHANICS:

1. Exploration: Explore a large interconnected world with abandoned cities, forests, military facilities, and underground locations.
2. Survival: Manage hunger, thirst, health, stamina, and temperature.
3. Combat: Use firearms, knives, melee weapons, and improvised weapons.
4. Inventory: Collect resources, ammunition, medicine, food, and crafting materials.
5. Crafting: Create weapons, tools, medical supplies, and survival equipment.
6. Character progression: Gain experience, unlock abilities, and improve survival skills.
7. NPC interactions: Meet survivors, merchants, hostile groups, and potential allies.
8. Choices and consequences: Decisions affect the story, characters, and different endings.
9. Quests: Include main missions, optional missions, and hidden discoveries.
10. Base building: Allow players to establish and improve a safe shelter.

COMBAT SYSTEM:

Implement a real-time 2D combat system with responsive controls, enemy AI, weapon variety, ammunition management, and realistic damage feedback.

STORY AND WORLD:

Create a mysterious and emotionally engaging storyline. The player must discover what caused the infection, uncover military secrets, and decide who deserves to survive.

Include different enemy types:

- Infected humans.
- Hostile survivors.
- Armed military groups.
- Dangerous mutated creatures.

USER INTERFACE:

Create a clean and immersive interface featuring:

- Health bar.
- Stamina bar.
- Hunger and thirst indicators.
- Inventory menu.
- Equipment menu.
- Quest journal.
- Interactive map.
- Character statistics.

AUDIO:

Use atmospheric background music, realistic environmental sounds, weapon sounds, footsteps, rain, wind, and enemy noises.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

- The game must be fully playable.
- Use a 2D side-scrolling perspective.
- Include smooth character movement.
- Implement functional menus and interactive objects.
- Create a save and load system.
- Optimize performance.
- Use modular and maintainable code.
- Make the game feel like a professional indie RPG.

IMPORTANT:

Do not create a simple prototype with static images. Build an actual playable game with functional mechanics, interactive environments, enemies, missions, progression, and a compelling story.

Prioritize realism, immersion, atmosphere, and gameplay quality.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Objective
- Build “ASHES OF TOMORROW,” a playable 2D side-scrolling post-apocalyptic survival RPG with exploration, combat, survival meters, missions, choices, UI, and saving.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game with responsive movement, enemy AI, interactive environments, inventory/crafting, progression, story choices, and save/load.
- Use a dark, cinematic visual style and support mobile touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game using HTML, CSS, Canvas, and localStorage.
- Assumed a single-player side-scrolling experience with a finite explorable world and a multi-step story ending in a consequential choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main game interface, responsive styling, HUD, title screen, modal panels, and mobile controls.
- Added Canvas rendering for the environment, player, enemies, weather, and world props.
- Added substantial gameplay/story logic in `game.js`: survival stats, inventory, crafting, weapons, enemies, quests, interactions, endings, and save/load scaffolding.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`; the file currently ends after the `update(dt)` function and is missing input/event wiring, the main animation loop, and initialization.
- Test the game in a browser, fix runtime issues, and verify gameplay/UI behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete `game.js` with keyboard/mouse/touch listeners, modal action delegation, pause/reload/interaction controls, and the animation loop calling `update()` and `render()`.
2. Initialize the title screen, HUD, quest, and loaded player state; ensure save/load and death/restart flows work.
3. Run the game locally and test movement, combat, missions, inventory, crafting, endings, and mobile layout; fix any issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, title screen, modal, and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Game state, rendering, survival/combat/story logic; unfinished at the end of `update(dt)`.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive layout.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no browser test or screenshot verification has been performed.
- `game.js` already defines `startGame`, `performAction`, `useItem`, `reload`, `update`, `render`, and other gameplay helpers, but they are not yet wired to events or a requestAnimationFrame loop.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the existing playable browser game “ASHES OF TOMORROW,” including gameplay, progression, UI, and saving.

## Requirements
- Responsive movement, enemy AI, interactive environments, inventory/crafting, progression, story choices, and save/load.
- Dark cinematic styling and mobile touch controls.

## Decisions
- Implement as a standalone browser game using HTML, CSS, Canvas, and localStorage.
- Use a finite side-scrolling world and a multi-step story ending in a consequential choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, HUD, title screen, modal panels, responsive styling, and mobile-control markup.
- Implemented rendering, gameplay, story progression, combat, survival meters, inventory/crafting, persistence, and input wiring.
- Added enemy reset behavior for restart and restored used-interactable state from saves.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Started a local HTTP server and opened the game in headless Chromium; captured the title screen at `/tmp/opencode/ashes-title.png`.

### Active
- Verify gameplay, progression, save/load, and mobile layout in-browser; fix issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction/runtime verification remains incomplete; only the initial title-screen capture was taken.

## Next Move
1. Use browser DevTools/CDP to inspect runtime errors and test start, movement, jumping, firing, interactions, and enemy behavior.
2. Test mission progression, choices/endings, inventory/crafting, pause, death/restart, and save/load.
3. Check mobile layout and touch controls; fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay, rendering, UI wiring, persistence, and initialization.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, modal, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive layout.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; the game files and supporting files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- Local server was started on port `8765`; headless Chromium was launched with remote debugging on port `9222`.
- Initial screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/ashes-title.png`.
